- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for risk aversion.  
- If sentiment has been consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 30-day horizon.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10% above prior peak for 3–5 days.  
- If news volume drops to 0 for 2+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to reflect reduced market activity.  
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (±0.33 or higher change) — increase forecast by 1–3% to capture momentum.  
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match true trend.  
- Mean reversion applies if price deviates >15% from 30-day moving average — bring forecast back toward average within 5–7 days.
